release_oracle.reference_build: Linux x86_64 Release (user decision): the reference behaviour of the port
release_oracle.debug_checks_absent: The installed config.h reads `#  if (0)` around `#define OPENMS_ASSERTIONS`; the driver's op log records 'OPENMS_ASSERTIONS not defined'.
release_oracle.host: ibminode06 (Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, AMD EPYC 7763), work dir /scratch/kohlbach/progress-format-readers-oracle
release_oracle.compiler: conda-forge x86_64-conda-linux-gnu-g++ 14.4.0 from the install's deps/, -O2 -std=c++20 -rdynamic, -lOpenMS with rpath to the install
release_oracle.method: Each case runs a reader twice on a fresh file object reading the inputs listed under fixtures and reused_fixtures: once with setLogType(GUI) and make_gui_progress_logger replaced by a factory for a recording backend, so every backend the reader reaches is recorded - the file's own, the fresh ones ConsensusXMLFile and FeatureXMLFile make for their handlers with setLogType(getLogType()), and MzMLHandler's thread_local pg_outer copy - with its arguments and the depth the wrapper passes; and once with setLogType(CMD), whose stdout bytes are cut out by file offset. Store cases load their input first with a separate reader of type NONE. After each run the op log records the return fields or the exception and ProgressLogger's static recursion depth (read and reset to 0 through a derived class). OPENMS_LOG_* output goes to a separate log file; the fatal-error stream still reaches stderr, which is recorded but not part of the fixture.
release_oracle.throttle: ProgressLogger::setProgress/nextProgress return early while last_invoke_ == time(nullptr) (ProgressLogger.cpp:244, :255). The driver defines time() itself and is linked with -rdynamic (build_info.txt: the driver exports `time`, libOpenMS.so imports `time@GLIBC_2.2.5`); every call returns a new second, so no set can be suppressed. The Rust replay uses a clock with the same property.
release_oracle.masking: The two timing texts of each '-- done [took X (CPU), Y (Wall)' line, and the ' @ <rate>/s' throughput when present, are replaced (extract.py). The node's work directory in exception messages becomes <W>, each repetition's output directory <W>/out. The size of the stored mzIdentML file, which embeds its creation time, is masked.
release_oracle.repetition_result: all three runs exit 0; the masked tables are identical; raw op logs and stdout differ only in the masked texts
findings: MS2File::load, MzIdentMLFile::load and ::store make no progress call; FeatureXMLFile::loadSize and a missing MGF file stop before the section.

An exception inside a section bypasses endProgress: no done line, the static depth stays raised; in the mzML case the file object's own command backend then refuses the next list start (StopWatch.cpp:43), which MzMLFile::safeParse_ reports as ParseError.
MzDataHandler's function-local static scan counter survives a failed load: a second file object's setProgress values continue from 2 and exceed the range.
MascotGenericFile::load reports is.tellg() = -1 after a last END IONS without a newline, which the command backend prints as an invalid progress value.
ConsensusXMLHandler resets progress_ to 0 at each section start, so its values are deterministic.
A metadata-only mzML load leaves pg_outer's section open (EndParsingSoftly at <spectrumList>).
